Me too… I felt this in my core.

There is nothing quite like that moment when it hits you… that you’ve been loving, showing up, and giving from such a genuine place… and the other person just doesn’t have the capacity to meet you there. It’s honestly a hard slap in the face.

I used to think if I just loved harder, showed up more, gave more… it would be matched. But not everyone loves like we love. Not everyone cares like we care. And that realization can feel both heartbreaking and eye-opening at the same time.

But you’re so right… it’s not about becoming less kind. It’s about becoming more aware.

Because those moments? They really do reveal everything. They show you who is aligned with your heart… and who was only benefiting from it.

And as hard as it is, there’s something powerful in that clarity. It helps you protect your energy, your peace, and your kindness for the people who truly deserve it 🤍

Me too… this hit hard.

It really is a slap in the face realizing not everyone loves or cares the way you do. I’ve learned the hard way you can’t give your heart to people who don’t value it.

And if you really want to see who your friends are… go through a hard time and see who actually reaches out.

That’s when everything becomes clear 🤍

Have you ever shown up for someone—really shown up—only to realize they didn’t value you the same way?

There’s a particular kind of disappointment that comes from giving your time, energy, and heart to someone who didn’t deserve access to it in the first place.

Kindness is a beautiful quality. It’s what builds friendships, strengthens communities, and makes people feel seen.

But kindness without discernment can leave you overextended, overlooked, and, at times, taken advantage of.

Sometimes, we give freely because that’s who we are. We assume others operate the same way. We believe their words. We defend them. We invest.

And then, at some point, something shifts.

You start to notice inconsistencies. Things don’t quite add up. The effort isn’t reciprocated. The energy feels… off.

The lesson isn’t to stop being kind.

It’s to recognize that not everyone is equipped to receive your kindness in the way you intend to give it.

Kindness is a strength—but it’s also something worth protecting.
